However back to the present. I am now a 2a supporting adult. I have guns for carry and to hunt. However now my 2 year old is old enough to pull a trigger. I was never taught as a child and I have no clue how to go about teaching her.

Edit: I'm not looking for training on how to teach my 2 year old to shoot, but to keep her from playing with firearms.
Looking for resources on how to teach young children about gun saftey.

Children learn in stages. When they are very young, the first step is to keep them from getting into mischief, and when they are older and have sufficient impulse control, they can be encouraged to participate to an appropriate extent.

Consider the things in your home that are dangerous to children - medicine bottles, electrical outlets, kitchen knives, and so on. Convincing the child not to touch these things is half the battle, and demystifying them - satisfying the child's natural curiosity about them - is the other half. When they know not to touch these things, and also don't have any particular interest in them, then they will be less inclined to get into trouble with them.

I was brought up as I imagine most gun-savvy kids were, in an environment where I was allowed (and encouraged) to touch any gun in the house and learn all about them, but only under supervision. It was also made very clear to me that it was a very major NO-NO to touch a gun without supervision. I recall being tested once or twice too, when a firearm was left out for me to find, to see if I would respond properly (leave it alone and get an adult).

Many kids have only a passing initial curiosity about guns and couldn't care less about them afterwards. Others are fascinated.

When the child is older - say, old enough to ride a bike confidently - and if the child still has an interest in shooting, then taking a class together is good next step.

If you have not had any formal training yourself, you'd likely benefit from it too. As an added bonus, your instructor would probably be able to offer some additional advice on how to bring kids up to speed as well:

http://www.nrainstructors.org/CourseCatalog.aspx
